fixture._purpose: Added 2026-09-13, F1-width-bar-reshoot unit (evidence-integrity re-shoot). Follow-up 2 of F1-width-bar-review.md found the two original shot sets above were captured at an explicit fillAngle:45 while the width/ink table in F1-width-bar-impl.md (JOB 2 / this file's width_measurements_mm_addLayer_rig and job1_discrepancy_resolution) was measured with fillAngle left absent -- a ~35-40% inkMm gap between the pictures and the numbers in the SAME report. This block states both fixtures explicitly and records what the gap actually turned out to be.

new_shots_addLayer_rig_measured_fixture.why_bespoke: scene3d-capture.js hardcodes fillAngle:45 as a literal in BOTH its create (line 313) and addLayer (line 280) construction branches, unconditionally, with no CLI flag to omit it. There is therefore NO cell in ANY gallery manifest, on either rig, shot at an unset fillAngle -- confirmed by reading the script source. Per the task brief, a bespoke scene was captured instead.
new_shots_addLayer_rig_measured_fixture.rig: addLayer -- IDENTICAL construction to tests/helpers/scene3d-ribbon-width.js's measureRibbonWidth() (engine.addLayer('scene3d'), primitive swapped on the seed object3d leaf, obj.params.style.params = { ...existing, toneLaw: law } -- no other key written)
new_shots_addLayer_rig_measured_fixture.density: med (fillDensity absent, resolves to 50 via scene3d.js's own finite(sp.fillDensity, 50) fallback -- the SAME numeric value 'med' pins explicitly, confirmed by exact-digit ink/width matches below)
new_shots_addLayer_rig_measured_fixture.camera: 'a' (DEFAULT_CAMERA, untouched -- ALGO_DEFAULTS.scene3d.camera is byte-identical to P.DEFAULT_CAMERA)

non_default_params.fillAngle: ABSENT (not written into obj.params.style.params at all) -- resolves via scene3d.js's own finite(sp.fillAngle, 45) fallback at generate() time. EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED to resolve to the SAME visible/numeric result as the original shots' explicit fillAngle:45 (see finding below) -- so despite being the literal difference the review flagged, fillAngle is NOT the cause of the inkMm gap.
non_default_params.ground: NOT hidden -- left at its ALGO_DEFAULTS default (sceneGround3d child visible, ground renders and casts a hatched shadow ellipse). This is the ONE deliberate construction choice that diverges from scene3d-capture.js's addLayer branch, chosen because it is exactly what measureRibbonWidth() (the function that produced every number in F1-width-bar-impl.md's tables) actually builds -- it never touches the ground child.

finding_2026-09-13_fillAngle_is_not_the_.summary: The ~35-40% inkMm gap the reviewer found is caused ENTIRELY by ground-plane inclusion, not by fillAngle. Proof: hiding the sceneGround3d child in the exact-same measured-fixture construction (fillAngle still absent, everything else unchanged) reproduces the ORIGINAL gallery addLayer-rig inkMm figures to the LAST PRINTED DIGIT for all four subject laws -- interlockWeave 3897.9, trochoidLoop 4303.7, onePenDown 3794.7, amplitudeOnly 1617.4, exactly matching manifest.B.1-1.addlayer.jsonl. The residual (measured minus ground-hidden) is 2269.0 / 2269.0 / 2269.0 / 2269.1 mm -- a CONSTANT additive amount across all four tone laws (the ground quad + the torus's own cast-shadow hatch ink, independent of the object's own tone-law pattern), not a per-law effect an angle change would produce.
finding_2026-09-13_fillAngle_is_not_the_.method: Ran the bespoke capture script's exact in-page construction twice: once as measureRibbonWidth() builds it (ground untouched) and once with an added `groundChild.visible = false` line (matching scene3d-capture.js's own addLayer-branch ground-hiding technique), both against the identical 42acff7b-sha scratch export, same port, same session.
finding_2026-09-13_fillAngle_is_not_the_.conclusion: fillAngle absent vs fillAngle:45 produce IDENTICAL ink and (where measurable) width numbers once ground is equalized -- this is a direct, measured proof that the algorithm's finite(sp.fillAngle, 45) fallback really does make an absent fillAngle behave as 45 for this fixture (torus/hatch), consistent with src/core/scene3d/params.js's SCENE_MIGRATIONS[2] comment ('a fresh hatch keeps the panel's 45 seed on a curved primitive'). The review's follow-up 2 correctly identified that the pictures and the numbers used different explicit constructions, and correctly declined to treat it as blocking -- but the SPECIFIC mechanism it named (fillAngle) is not the actual cause; ground-plane inclusion is.

fixture.visual_diff_2026-09-13: Looked at torus__hatch__onePenDown__med__a__addlayer.webp (original, 800x400, ground hidden) vs torus__hatch__onePenDown__med__a__addlayer__measured.png (new, 800x561, ground shown) at native resolution. The torus itself -- the actual measured object -- is visually indistinguishable between the two: same thin zigzag-tooth ribbon pattern, same ~11 CLS_RIBBON stretches' worth of visible gaps, same overall wireframe-like read. The new capture additionally shows a large ellipse below the torus: the ground plane, rendered with straight diagonal hatch lines (the ground's own fill/shadow pattern, unrelated to the torus's toneLaw), which the original excludes by design (scene3d-capture.js hides the ground child for a clean object-only crop). This ground ellipse is the entire source of the extra ~2269mm of ink and the ~561px vs ~400px taller crop -- not a change in the torus's own rendering.

what_i_saw: onePenDown, both rigs: the ring's ribbons are thin zigzag lines with visible black gaps between successive teeth -- a wireframe-like read, not a bold filled band. This matches the 'thin wireframe zigzags' description that raised decision 10, and is consistent with this unit's own measured mean CLS_RIBBON width of 0.88mm (2.93 pen widths) on this fixture -- thinner than the pre-F1-amp 1.01mm (3.36 pen) and thinner still than F1-placement's own pre-fix numbers (F1-erode-plan.md Section 7: 1.03mm at 8adfd5af).
